correctness.rationale: For \(q\ge2\) and \(n\ge2\), the cyclic-gap parametrization enumerates all primitive weight-two necklaces. Cyclic rotations cannot both occur in a non-overlapping code. Unequal gaps supply \(\lfloor(n-1)/2\rfloor(q-1)^2\) classes. At even \(n=2m+2\), for any two tied-gap words \(0^i a0^m b0^{m-i}\) and \(0^j c0^m d0^{m-j}\), equality \(a=d\) induces a proper overlap of length \(m+i-j+1\); the first- and last-color supports are disjoint and their product is at most \(\lfloor(q-1)^2/4\rfloor\). The all-unbalanced larger-initial-gap construction, augmented by a balanced color bipartition for tied gaps, is non-overlapping because a matching prefix/suffix would require the initial zero gap to be no greater than the prefinal zero gap and the marker colors to agree. This is impossible except across tied words, where color sets are disjoint. The empty boundary \(n=q=2\) is included. A standalone checker passed 91 constructed parameter cases/438,536 ordered pair comparisons plus 20 exact full-conflict-graph mixed-integer optima for \(2\le q\le5\) and \(2\le n\le6\). Experiments corroborate but do not establish the infinite proof.

Exact two-nonzero all-parameter q-ary capacity, and specifically the even-length bipartite deficit, was not covered by examined general constructions, integer programs, balanced/run-limited studies or binary higher-weight code results. The novelty assessment is qualified by unindexed possible equivalences, rather than an assertion of global priority.
residual_risks: An equivalent constant-weight-two result may exist in unindexed code theory or a paper appendix not located by targeted source/alias searches.

value.rationale: This is a natural fixed-support synchronization coding optimum for every alphabet and block length, with a sharp and structurally motivated odd/even necklace-packing dichotomy. It provides explicit optimal constructions and exposes the first strict gap at \(q=4\), \(n\) even, by a forced bipartite split of two colored markers. The exact broad family resolves more than a small table, renaming, or a direct application of the known \(n=2\) alphabet partition.
